Five interactive diagrams mapping the Week 3 syllabus: animate the derivation of a demand curve step by step, decompose price changes into substitution and income effects, explore income shifts, drill shift-vs-movement, and map cross-price effects.

Five figures for the Week 3 syllabus: build a demand curve from her choices, split a price change into substitution and income effects, shift demand with income, tell a shift from a movement, and map cross-price effects. Each figure asks one question. Answer it on the graph by tapping or dragging (your guess shows in plum), then press Reveal and watch the answer draw itself in. Point at a graph to read the numbers under the pointer; a dragged point always shows where it is.

Every price of X pins down one optimal bundle in the Utility Maximization panel. Now let's change the price of X and see what changes. That bundle's X-coordinate is then plotted in the Demand Curve panel below it, building the demand curve one point at a time.

§ 3.1

Two-Panel Demand Derivation

Every price of X pins down one optimal bundle in the utility maximization panel. Now let's change the price of X and see what changes. As the price falls, the budget line pivots outward, the consumer reaches a new indifference curve, and a new optimal point emerges. That bundle's X-coordinate is then plotted in the demand panel below it, building the demand curve one point at a time. Watch the film, then find one of those points yourself in Fig 3.1 below: pull the dashed indifference curve until it just touches the new budget line.
